questions.q: Examine the main causes of the French Revolution.
answer: The French Revolution of 1789 was the result of many long-standing grievances.

answer.text: France was an absolute monarchy under Louis XVI, and years of costly wars and royal extravagance had brought the state to a deep financial crisis.

Society was divided into three estates. The clergy and nobility, the first two estates, enjoyed privileges and paid almost no taxes, while the Third Estate — peasants, workers and the middle class — bore the entire burden of taxation.
Enlightenment thinkers such as Rousseau, Montesquieu and Voltaire spread ideas of liberty, equality and the separation of powers, which made people question the old order.

answer: These political, social and intellectual causes together sparked the Revolution.

questions.q: Describe the major events of the French Revolution and its legacy.

answer.text: In 1789 the Third Estate formed the National Assembly and took the Tennis Court Oath. On 14 July 1789 a crowd stormed the Bastille prison. The Declaration of the Rights of Man proclaimed liberty and equality, and a constitutional monarchy was set up in 1791. In 1792 the monarchy was abolished and France became a Republic; Louis XVI was executed in 1793. Under Robespierre and the Jacobins came the Reign of Terror, with mass executions by the guillotine.
The Revolution spread the motto Liberty, Equality, Fraternity. Napoleon later carried its laws across Europe. It inspired democracy, nationalism and human rights across the world.
